design.affected_system: public-sector analytical, scoring, triage, optimization, and human-review systems
alternatives: add targeted redundancy around the largest failure modes in algorithmic decision support under technical and institutional failure
select an adaptive robust portfolio across severe scenarios for algorithmic decision support under technical and institutional failure
pair data, model, interface, human, vendor, attack, and capacity failure simulation with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Model output, recommendation, human decision, action, appeal, service, and outcome remain distinct.
High-impact decisions require lawful authority, human responsibility, contestability, and incident response.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: apply current continuity provisions to algorithmic decision support under technical and institutional failure.

constraints.description: The algorithmic decision support and governance stress test must respect declared minimum continuity and safety thresholds across severe scenarios.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: algorithmic accountability officer and responsible technology review board
design.decision_question: Which controls preserve lawful service under drift, missingness, manipulation, outage, override, and demand surge?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The algorithmic decision support and governance stress test must respect declared minimum continuity and safety thresholds across severe scenarios.
independence_key.decision_object: algorithmic decision support under technical and institutional failure
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for algorithmic decision support under technical and institutional failure passes documented checks for scenario ranges, dependence, failure rates, recovery, intervention performance, and sensitivity.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: data, model, interface, human, vendor, attack, and capacity failure simulation
independence_key.primary_outcome: scenario-weighted high-impact decisions outside safe fallback

design.intended_claim: A versioned stress-test design for comparing declared alternatives affecting algorithmic decision support under technical and institutional failure, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: scenario-weighted high-impact decisions outside safe fallback
distributional gap in scenario-weighted high-impact decisions outside safe fallback
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not present synthetic failures, decisions, affected people, or harms as observed incidents.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for algorithmic decision support under technical and institutional failure passes documented checks for scenario ranges, dependence, failure rates, recovery, intervention performance, and sensitivity.

design.title: Stress-test algorithmic systems and human fallback
transportability_risks: Law, institutional process, data-generating systems, populations, incentives, and recourse differ.
Technical fairness metrics may conflict and cannot establish legal or substantive fairness alone.

family.affected_system: public-sector analytical, scoring, triage, optimization, and human-review systems
claim_boundary: Area and administrative differences do not establish discrimination, preferences, or individual behavior.
Behavioral and allocation designs require rights, accessibility, privacy, and non-coercion review.
Causal, fairness, adoption, and welfare claims require direct outcomes and independent governance evidence.
family.decision_owner: algorithmic accountability officer and responsible technology review board
family.description: Eight decisions for system diagnosis, workload forecasting, control portfolios, review siting, oversight allocation, audit scheduling, failure stress, and causal system evaluation.
family.title: Algorithmic decision support and governance

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
